chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: Getting into Billy Rose's Carmen Jones as Rum and Dink, despite Nazarro
summary: Rose wanted a name act for comedians Rum and Dink; Nazarro hid the call and sent Heckle and Jive, but Bubbles made his own appointment and signed the contract.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: time that Billy Rose was opening up his show in Philadelphia called "Carmen Jones."

'32, I think it was, '32 or '33. However -- so we wanted to get -- the show got a good write-up, there was good costumes and good story but they had no names in the show, the character show. So that means Billy Rose wanted to get a name act to put in. So he had a spot -- they could use a comedy team for two comedians in the show called Rum and Dink. Rum and Dink was the name of the comedians that he had in the show and he'd figured he'd get Buck and Bubbles and name them Rum and Dink and they'd have a name act.
Was it all white except for --
All colored. All colored. It was called "Carmen Jones."

Yeah, that was it. I was just trying to think of Erskine Miller, he was a prize fighter. So when Lou Leslie came back to New York after opening up in Philadelphia he looked for Buck and Bubbles. We were at the Paramount and he called the theater to talk to me and I told him he had to talk to my manager who was Nazarro. So what happened is that when we were playing the Paramount Theater we got a call -- we were booked up for two weeks -- we got a call from Billy Rose's office that he wanted to know if we would be able to go in his show and he had to have a talk with us, he had to call my manager, I gave him the phone number to call Nat Nazarro and he'd let him know. So that day went down and Nazarro's office didn't call us to tell us that he had gotten no word from Billy Rose or nothing.

But he doesn't know the idea of Billy Rose was fool enough to call in for us. So the day goes down. So the next day I figure, why this guy ain't told me nothing about Billy Rose calling. Wonder what his story is. So I called the office to ask him if there was any mail -- no mail. Anybody call for us? No. By that time Nazarro is on the other phone -- he heard me say "nobody called" "No." Then he got on the phone to answer. So I said, "Did you get a call from Billy Rose?" Now they don't know I know that Billy Rose got their number and he was going to call to find out. Now he tells me on the phone -- "Billy Rose -- he's a cheap guy he don't want to pay no money." "Really?" But you never told me you got a call from him. "No, he don't want to pay no money," says he.

Now in the meantime he's sent Heckle and Jive over to get the job and they've already received the script to do the part and he told Billy Rose that we were engaged for future bookings somewhere else. This was our
last week. We only got two weeks at the Paramount and then we ain't got no more booking. But that's what he did.

Okay. When the show was over that day -- no, before the show was over, I tell "Why you know the man ain't got no money," says I to him, "he's cheap." "He only will pay $100." "How do you know how he going to pay, he ain't going to ask for Buck and Bubbles and pay no money, I don't think that." That's what I tell him. He says, "You know I'm looking out for you." I says, "I know you are. That's why I'm asking now. Why you say that he don't want to pay no money. Did you ask him?" "Why don't you make an appointment and let's go see him." He say, "You make the appointment." Nazarro tells me to make the appointment. Well, I've already made the appointment. He don't know that. I made the appointment to see Billy Rose, understand? So I wasn't going to tell him that on the phone. So I said, all right, I'll make the appointment.

So the next day I got the appointment for 3 o'clock. So I call up the next day to the office and tell Nazarro I've got an appointment for us for 3 o'clock this afternoon with Billy Rose. Okay. You don't tell me he's got any kind of a job or nothing, you know that. Billy Rose tells me that, you know. He told me that the next day because he says to me, he says, he told me you were booked up and you were busy and he sent Heckle and Jive the book and over. I gave them the script. I said, "Did ya? I said, "We've got an appointment for 3 o'clock, right?"

Okay. When I get Nazarro and Buck over to his office, Billy Rose office in the Ziegfeld Theater, that's where his office was, we get in his office and Buck and Nazarro didn't say a word 'cause I did all the talking. I introduced Nat and I introduced Buck to Billy Rose and I started talking about the show and the possibilities of Buck and I going in the show, we ain't doing nothing and I got the contract.

All he had to do is okay the contract, sign the contract, that's all I let him do. Sing the contract, we were going in the show. That's how I got in "Carmen Jones." I got in the Ziegfeld Follies almost the same way. However, so we go get the contract signed, go in the show and success in the show, okay? Then this is 1931, I think it is -- 1930 --
